from.place: ## Proof, first sentence: the proper curve C must first be shown projective, using the dimension-one quasi-projectivity input; via Stacks 09NZ, proof, second sentence: 'By Lemma 09NX the scheme Z [the reduction of X] has an ample invertible sheaf'

title: A Noetherian reduced separated scheme of dimension at most one has an ample invertible module
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] which is Noetherian (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]), reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and separated (the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]), and whose underlying topological space has Krull dimension $\dim X\le1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] ($X=\varnothing$ allowed). Then there exists an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$ [def-sc-invertible-module] which is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Varieties, Lemma 09NX (varieties-lemma-dim-1-noetherian-reduced-separated-has-ample, line 8080), stated there for dimension 1; its proof uses Lemma 09ND (varieties-lemma-dim-1-noetherian-integral-separated-has-ample, line 7927), Lemma 09NE (varieties-lemma-glue-invertible-sheaves), Remark 09NW (varieties-remark-conductor), Properties Lemma 09NV (properties-lemma-ample-finite-set-in-principal-affine), Limits Lemma 09NL (limits-lemma-affines-glued-in-closed-affine), Properties Proposition 01Q3 (properties-proposition-characterize-ample) and Properties Lemma 01PV (properties-lemma-affine-cap-s-open); the case dim X <= 1 is the one Lemma 0A25 needs

proof.text: If dim X ≤ 0, take the tensor unit and the existing dimension-zero affineness and ampleness theorem. This includes the empty scheme.

Use component_intersections_finite to enumerate the components via Fintype.equivFin. Give each its vanishing-ideal subscheme structure. The proved source-library reducedness instance and Mathlib irreducible-subspace result make each integral; closed immersion gives inherited Noetherianity, separatedness and dimension bound. If its dimension is ≤0 use the zero-dimensional theorem; otherwise ENat.WithBot.add_one_le_iff and the bound show dimension=1, so use the integral theorem. Choose ample modules on the components. Identify T with the union of intersections in the enumeration.
Apply the glued component affine section theorem to obtain L with ample component restrictions and an affine first-power section locus U containing T.

For x in T use the section of U. Otherwise component_intersections_finite and injectivity of the enumeration give a unique component index containing x. Apply the component-supported affine section theorem to obtain a positive-power affine section locus through x. Rewrite each locus equality into the defining pointwise germ equivalence of IsAmple. CompactSpace X is already an assumption, so this proves IsAmple X L.

proof_origin.place: 09NX, full proof, with dimension-zero components handled by Properties 0AAX and 0CKV; steps 3-4 and 5-7 extracted to two intermediate statements by M1
